title: Top Account Feature Auction and Acceptance Signals
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Background: As Redwood scales, VIP customers frequently request features that compete for limited roadmap space. Current intake channels surface qualitative urgency but lack a consistent, measurable signal that product and sales can use to make tradeoffs in a single sprint. This ticket proposes a lightweight "feature auction" mechanism paired with an acceptance-signal rubric to translate commercial urgency into prioritizable, measurable inputs for the roadmap.

Goals: 1) Create a repeatable intake flow where top accounts can express prioritized asks via credit-weighted requests or impact statements. 2) Define a small set of quantitative acceptance signals (usage projections, expected revenue retention, integration complexity score, regulatory lift) that feed a prioritization score. 3) Build an internal dashboard and acceptance calculator that returns a ranked list and a recommended delivery commitment (canary, A/B, or full). 4) Provide guardrails to prevent gaming and ensure fairness across accounts.

Scope (in): intake form, credit allocation model, acceptance-signal rubric, prioritization calculator prototype, internal dashboard view, beta rollout to 5 strategic accounts, documentation and training for GTM.

Scope (out): automated billing or contractual changes, public-facing marketplace, major backend runtime changes. Those may follow after successful pilot.

Success criteria: - Pilot with 5 accounts yields at least 3 prioritized features that pass the rubric and are scheduled into a sprint within the quarter. - Product and Sales report >30% reduction in sync time for escalation alignment. - Measurable post-release acceptance metrics captured in console (usage uplift, retention delta) for at least 2 features.

Acceptance criteria: - Intake form deployed in Confluence + linkable short URL. - Credit allocation rules documented and approved by Sales and Finance. - Prioritization calculator (spreadsheet or small internal web UI) that computes composite score from acceptance signals. - Dashboard card in Console showing top-accounts queued feature requests and status. - Pilot run with 3-5 accounts and retrospective notes captured.

Proposed approach: 1) Define credit model: each strategic customer gets X credits per quarter (based on ARR band). Credits are spent to elevate the priority of an ask; a minimum credit threshold qualifies an ask for product review. 2) Acceptance signals: standardized inputs (expected monthly active users impacted, estimated ARR retention/protection, implementation complexity (T-shirt), security/regulatory lift, strategic dependency multiplier). 3) Scoring: weighted sum configurable by PMs; initial weights proposed and reviewed with revenue ops. 4) Implementation: build a Figma intake screen + Confluence intake page; a Google Sheet prototype with scoring; iterate to a minimal internal web UI if sheet proves limiting. 5) Controls: cap credits, cooling period, and a manual override for exec escalations.

Tradeoffs and risks: - Risk of sales gaming credits -> mitigation: finance oversight and audit logs, quarterly reset. - Adds administrative overhead for Sales/Customer Success -> mitigation: simple form, education and concierge support for first two quarters. - Might bias roadmap toward high-ARR customers -> mitigation: include product-fit/market-signal weight and reserve slots for low-touch, high-leverage platform work.

Stakeholders: PM (Sofia Patel), Sales lead: Marco Alvarez, RevOps: Priya Menon, Engineering partner: Jared Kim, Design: Elena Morozova, Legal: Grace Lin.

Milestones: - Week 1-2: finalize scoring rubric and credit tiers. - Week 3: build Confluence intake and Sheet prototype. - Week 4-6: pilot with 3 accounts + collect feedback. - Week 7-9: iterate on weighting and build minimal web UI + console card. - Week 10: retrospective and decision to scale or sunset.

Artifacts & links: Confluence PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/FEATURE-AUCTION-PRD (draft); Prototype sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/feature-auction-proto; Figma intake mock: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/feature-auction; Pilot tracker (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/feature-auction-pilot; GitHub infra repo (placeholder for UI work): https://github.com/redwood-inference/feature-auction.

Next steps: schedule alignment sync with Sales/RevOps, finalize weight matrix and credit formula, prepare pilot communication to 5 accounts, and create dashboard spec for Console team.
